headline: Forest’s shot volume fails to translate into more than a draw at Ipswich

sentences.text: Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest shared the points in a 1–1 draw, with both goals arriving before half-time and neither side scoring after the break.
Nottingham Forest struck first in the 13th minute, when Neco Williams scored with Daniel Muñoz providing the assist.
Ipswich restored parity in the 41st minute through Julio Enciso, leaving the teams level at the interval.
The statistical profile points to a substantial gap between Forest’s attacking volume and the final score.
Forest recorded 17 shots to Ipswich’s 7 and produced 2.29 expected goals against 0.46, a difference of 1.83 xG.
The visitors also led 5–3 in shots on target and 2–1 in big chances, while winning 5 corners to Ipswich’s 0.
Possession was almost even, with Forest at 50.6% and Ipswich at 49.4%; passing totals were similarly close at 480 and 486 respectively.
Ipswich’s 3 goalkeeper saves, compared with Forest’s 2, and the 11 Forest attempts off target underline how the visitors generated pressure without converting it into a winning margin.
The formations were 4-2-3-1 for Ipswich and 3-4-2-1 for Forest.
Ipswich entered with 6 points from their previous 5 league matches, while Forest had taken 4 from their preceding 5.
The draw moved Ipswich from 10th before kick-off to 9th, with 10 points from 8 matches.
Forest climbed from 19th to 16th, taking their total to 6 points from 8 matches.
